chunks: Ibn Idris, from his father, from Ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked: By what did you know your Lord? He said: By the dissolution of resolution and the invalidation of plan. I resolved but He dissolved my resolution, and I planned but He invalidated my plan.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq know his Lord according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the experiential dissolution of one's own firm resolutions (faskh al-'azm) as the primary means of knowing God, illustrating the transition from self-reliance to total dependence on the Divine. This concept, rooted in the Shia tradition of 'tawhid al-a'mal' (unity of action), emphasizes that recognizing God's power to invalidate human intent serves as a practical proof of His sovereignty and presence in daily life. The narration underscores that true gnosis arises not merely from intellectual assent but from the lived experience of divine intervention in one's affairs.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/298] al-Tawhid: Ibn Idris – his father – Ibn Hashim – Ibn Abi Umayr – Hisham b. Salim who said:

Abu Abdillah عليه السلام was asked: By what (thing) did you know your Lord? He said: By the dissolution of resolutions and the invalidation of plans. I resolved but He dissolved my resolution and I planned but He invalidated my plan.
